artworks.title: Prometheus Bound
artworks.description: Rubens dramatizes the sentence Hesiod and Apollodorus impose for the theft of fire: Prometheus nailed to the rock while an eagle feeds on his regenerating liver. The painting pairs the Titan's punishment with the earlier deed — the hollow fennel stalk and mankind's flame — that made Zeus hide fire and Pandora inevitable.

artworks.title: Prometheus Bringing Fire to Mankind
artworks.description: A neoclassical allegory of the fennel-stalk theft in Hesiod Theogony 565–567 and Works and Days 47–52: Prometheus descends with the far-seen gleam of unwearying fire while mortals reach upward from the darkness Zeus had imposed after the trick at Mecone.
